LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen nearly 30% from its high — unusually steep for a steady defense company — but it's a company-specific slump, not a sign that military spending is slowing down.

ASML.sentence: ASML has drifted down about 24% from its peak, which is just a breather for the only company on earth that makes a certain essential chip-printing machine — the underlying demand hasn't gone away.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quietly doing its job while the market gets nervous — investors tend to hide in steady businesses like industrial gas when they're worried, and Linde's long-term supply contracts make it exactly that kind of safe harbor.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is calm — it's dipped a bit from its high, but the cloud-and-AI story just keeps grinding along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is sitting right about where it's been, having recovered most of an earlier slump — it supplies the equipment nearly every lab and biotech company needs, so it tends to move with the broad health of research spending.

CVX.sentence: Chevron is steady, and while its profits look fat right now, that's mostly because fighting near Iran has pushed oil prices well above normal rather than anything the company itself did — at an ordinary oil price it's fairly valued, not a bargain.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen sharply — down almost half from its high — which is a big enough drop that it may reflect real worries about growth, even though big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its workflow and AI-automation tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore has lagged the broader copper rally a bit lately, but this miner-and-trader still moves with the prices of copper and the other metals it digs up and deals in.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta edged up, and the thing that matters most — the price it gets per ton of crushed stone — is still rising a few percent a year, exactly as this quarry business is built to do.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is flat, with a slightly weaker Mexican peso nibbling at the value once its earnings are converted into dollars — otherwise nothing much is happening with this Latin American Coke bottler.

UBER.sentence: Uber is steady, and the number that matters most — how many rides people are booking — is still growing briskly with no sign yet that self-driving cars are pulling business away.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, is trading below what it would cost to replace its own fleet of ships — an unusually cheap level for a company whose fortunes track global trade.

MA.sentence: Mastercard ticked up, and interestingly it's trading at only a slim premium to Visa right now, smaller than usual — meanwhile people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so the business itself is humming.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical-robot company is down nearly 29% from its high, but hospitals are still on track to do more procedures this year — and each operation sells more of the instruments and supplies that are the real moneymaker.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia is holding steady, but the real question hanging over it is that two of its biggest customers — Google's parent and Amazon — are now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the difference, so whether those customers can keep paying is what matters most, not anything about Nvidia's own chips.
